raw_case_text: In July 2022, a 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with SLE, lupus nephritis, and polyserositis. She presented with symptoms of facial edema, anorexia, nausea, abdominal distention, cough, and white phlegm. The severity of her condition was measured using the SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI), which scored 20. Initially, the patient received treatment with glucocorticoids (methylprednisolone, prednisone), immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, mycophenolate mofetil), and hydroxychloroquine sulfate. After confirming no contraindications such as infection or allergies, the patient began receiving belimumab (480mg) on July 22, 2022. Four rounds of therapy were completed by September 29, 2022. During this period, the patient's symptoms gradually improved, and her SLEDAI score decreased. As a result, the dosage of glucocorticoids and mycophenolate mofetil was gradually reduced. However, in October, the patient developed an infection with the herpes zoster virus. Although she did not experience a noticeable cough or expectoration, she had occasional chest tightness and mild shortness of breath. Before the fifth belimumab therapy, on November 1, 2022, a chest computed tomography scan revealed patchy, nodular, and flocculent ground-glass density shadows in all lung lobes, as well as nodules and cavities in the dorsal segment of the left lower lobe. These findings indicated pulmonary infiltration associated with SLE and pulmonary infectious lesions (Figure 1a and b). HIV and anti-IFN-gamma autoantibody test results were negative. White blood count and C-reactive protein were normal. Serum beta-D-glucan, serum galactomannan, cryptococcal capsular antigen, tuberculosis antibody, candida IgG antibody and candida antigen test were negative. CD4+T lymphocyte count was 332/ul (reference range, 180-324/ul), CD8+T lymphocyte count was 646/ul (reference range, 1185-1901/ul), absolute NK cell count was 16/ul (reference range, 200-587/ul), IgG 5.44 g/L (reference range, 8-18g/L), IgA 1.16g/L (reference range, 0.9-4.5g/L), IgM 0.64g/L (reference range, 0.84-1.32g/L). The next generation sequencing (NGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) showed that Pneumocystis jirovecii (sequence number 178940) and Talaromyces marneffei (sequence number 7480). TM was cultured from the patients' BALF (Figure 2a and b). Meanwhile, BALF was positive for PJ by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Finally, we discontinued the fifth belimumab therapy. Voriconazole (0.6g/d on day 1 and 0.4g/d from day 2) was used to treat TM infection. She had a history of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. Therefore, PJ pneumonia was treated with clarithromycin 1.8g/d for the first week. Our test for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase was normal. Clarithromycin was changed to sulfamethoxazole. The treatment of SLE, maintenance of prednisone 5mg/d, MMF 0.75g/d, hydroxychloroquine sulfate 0.2g/d. After about one month of therapy, the reexamination of chest computed tomography showed that the pneumonia was improved (Figure 1c and d). The patient is still under follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 52-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presented in November 2022 with occasional chest tightness and mild shortness of breath following a recent herpes zoster infection.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In July 2022, the patient was diagnosed with SLE, lupus nephritis, and polyserositis (SLEDAI score 20) after presenting with facial edema, anorexia, nausea, abdominal distension, cough, and white sputum. She was treated with glucocorticoids (methylprednisolone, prednisone), cyclosporine, mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), hydroxychloroquine, and four infusions of belimumab (480 mg initiated July 22, 2022 through September 29, 2022), which improved her symptoms and allowed tapering of glucocorticoids and MMF. In October 2022, she developed herpes zoster infection followed by occasional chest tightness and mild dyspnea prior to her scheduled fifth belimumab dose on November 1, 2022.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus nephritis and polyserositis diagnosed in July 2022; history of reported glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; herpes zoster infection in October 2022.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for occasional chest tightness and mild shortness of breath; negative for noticeable cough or expectoration in November 2022. Home medications included tapered prednisone, mycophenolate mofetil, hydroxychloroquine sulfate, and belimumab.

objective.routine_investigations: WBC count and CRP were normal. HIV serology and anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies were negative. Serum beta-D-glucan, galactomannan, cryptococcal capsular antigen, tuberculosis antibody, Candida IgG antibody, and Candida antigen tests were all negative. Serum immunoglobulins showed decreased IgG at 5.44 g/L (reference 8–18 g/L), normal IgA at 1.16 g/L (reference 0.9–4.5 g/L), and decreased IgM at 0.64 g/L (reference 0.84–1.32 g/L). Repeat G6PD enzyme testing was normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Lymphocyte subset analysis revealed CD4+ T-cell count 332/µL (reference 180–324/µL), reduced CD8+ T-cell count 646/µL (reference 1185–1901/µL), and markedly depleted NK cell count 16/µL (reference 200–587/µL). Chest CT (November 1, 2022) demonstrated diffuse bilateral patchy, nodular, and flocculent ground-glass opacities across all lung lobes, alongside nodules and cavitary lesions in the dorsal segment of the left lower lobe. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) next-generation sequencing (NGS), fungal culture, and PCR were performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Pulmonary co-infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii and Talaromyces marneffei in an HIV-negative immunocompromised 52-year-old woman with SLE receiving belimumab and immunosuppressive therapy. Definitive confirmation was achieved via BALF metagenomic NGS detecting Pneumocystis jirovecii (178,940 sequence reads) and Talaromyces marneffei (7,480 sequence reads), positive BALF P. jirovecii PCR, and positive BALF fungal culture isolating T. marneffei, while HIV and anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies were negative. The fifth dose of belimumab was discontinued, and SLE maintenance was adjusted to prednisone 5 mg/day, mycophenolate mofetil 0.75 g/day, and hydroxychloroquine 0.2 g/day. T. marneffei was treated with voriconazole (0.6 g/day on day 1, then 0.4 g/day), and P. jirovecii pneumonia was treated initially with clarithromycin 1.8 g/day for 1 week due to historical G6PD deficiency concern, then switched to sulfamethoxazole after normal G6PD activity was confirmed. Repeat chest CT after 1 month demonstrated marked radiographic improvement, and the patient remained stable on outpatient follow-up.
